critique: The orange/yellow color and brief rightward motion are closer to a muzzle-flash palette, but both frames still read as a compact cluster of overlapping soft blobs. There is no crisp bright yellow-white ignition core, no clearly separated fast particles, and no elongated directional flame/explosive spray. The 0.01 and 0.08 frames remain similarly sized and rounded rather than resolving into a sharp transient burst traveling to the right.

suggestions.why: Reducing the active burst from 20000/sec to 1500/sec leaves visible individual particles instead of merging hundreds of simultaneous particles into a uniform puff.
Lower particle feather makes the burst edges and separated particles read sharper, rather than as soft round blobs.
Shift the particle base toward hot yellow to establish the bright ignition portion of the muzzle flash while retaining orange variation.
